# talkdown

> talkdown is a small, no-install slide engine and Markdown format built for agents. A deck is one HTML file with Markdown in a `<script type="text/markdown">` block, loaded through https://sambhav.dev/talkdown/latest.js for automatic runtime updates, or direct deck.css/deck.js links for offline or pinned decks. Slides are the default on desktop and mobile. Article view turns shared speaker notes into prose; phones have visible Previous/Next buttons that move through steps and then slides, without extra inline navigation bars, and a menu containing Slides / Article, Home, and a section/slide picker. Native scrolling and browser gestures remain enabled; there is no custom swipe or edge-tap navigation. A `?view=read#section-id` link opens the article at a named section. The runtime supplies layout and interaction, keeping the authored source compact and editable by hand. Link cards use `::: links` around `- [Title](URL) Description` items, showing authored titles, domains and descriptions without metadata requests. Browser (`::: browser url="…"`), window (`::: window title="…"`) and phone (`::: phone`) frames wrap screenshots, code or Markdown in theme-aware CSS chrome. Simple `::: flow` and `::: stack` blocks turn bulleted lists into theme-native process boxes or top-to-bottom layers, without external rendering. `::: flow vertical` points down; slide `build: true` or item `{.step}` markers reveal boxes on ↓ and article view shows all items. Built-in components share the selected theme, and custom HTML and JavaScript can join the deck's navigation. Charts cover bar, horizontal bar, line, donut, heatmap, scatter, bubble, waterfall, timeline, Sankey, treemap and range, all from one Markdown table or CSV. Readers can click a Mermaid diagram or a chart to open it full screen and zoom. A `<div id="bar">` in the page (a `.title` plus links) replaces the default top bar.

Speaker cards use `::: speaker` around an optional photo, one `### Name`, role text and Markdown links; the same card becomes a compact article author box.

Write notes in `::: notes` / `::: say` / `::: read` blocks and charts in `::: chart` containers with plain numbers. Use one HTML file by default; a referenced Markdown file works when served over HTTP.

## Agent instructions

- [talkdown skill](https://sambhav.dev/talkdown/skills/talkdown/SKILL.md): how to write a deck: boilerplate, syntax, widgets, themes, rules, example. Read this first.
- [talkdown skill (jsDelivr)](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/sambhav/talkdown@main/skills/talkdown/SKILL.md): same file, via CDN.

## Docs and examples

- Roadmap boards: `::: board` with `###` column headings and Markdown lists of cards. ↓ reveals columns in slides; articles show every card, with columns stacked on phones. Syntax and examples are in the skill and widget gallery.

- [README](https://github.com/sambhav/talkdown/blob/main/README.md): setup instructions, authoring recommendations, syntax, widgets and themes.
- [Live demo](https://sambhav.dev/talkdown/): a short presentation about why the format exists, followed by live component examples and an authoring tour.
- [Widget gallery](https://sambhav.dev/talkdown/gallery.html): every widget and chart type, live, with its Markdown.
- [Starter deck](https://sambhav.dev/talkdown/examples/starter.html): a minimal template to copy.


latest.js loads the current release each time a page opens, so published decks never need updating. Custom scripts use Talkdown.onReady(Deck => { ... }). For offline or pinned decks, link deck.js and deck.css directly (download them from sambhav.dev/talkdown or a GitHub release).

HTTP exchanges use a `http` fence: request line, headers/body, a blank line, then the response status line and headers/body. Present view reveals the response on ↓; article view stacks both with Copy buttons.
